findings.claim: The stamp format is undefined, including glyph mappings, drop and sideload markers, multi-tile footprints, placement anchor, and rotation pivot.
findings.failure_scenario: Two implementations accept different stamp files and place the same furnace at different coordinates after rotation, while both pass their own parser and rotation tests; docs/conventions.md defines engine coordinates but does not resolve these choices.

findings.claim: The required burner-smelting demonstration has no specified mechanism for transferring gathered fuel and materials into machines.
findings.failure_scenario: Claude gathers and crafts the required items and builds every ghost, but the burner machines remain unfueled because walk, mine, craft, inv, and build provide no inventory-transfer operation; completing the demonstration requires manual intervention or additional behavior.

findings.claim: No acceptance criterion requires every layout to receive all three checks before construction.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation exposes look, shot, lint, and build as unrelated commands and immediately builds an unchecked plan, satisfying the command criteria while violating the mandatory draft-check-build sequence.

findings.claim: The supporting mine and craft commands have no acceptance requirements enforcing the Goal's reach, inventory, and fair-play constraints.
findings.failure_scenario: mine extracts resources from arbitrary distant coordinates or craft queues recipes without consuming ingredients, yet the stated supporting-command observations pass because explicit reach and item-consumption checks cover only build.

findings.claim: Lint does not define valid sources and sinks, intentional terminal outputs, or whether planned ghosts count as connected equipment.
findings.failure_scenario: One implementation accepts an inserter dropping onto a planned belt while another flags it because no real belt exists; an intentional output belt may also be indistinguishable from an accidentally disconnected belt.

findings.claim: Plan-dependent commands require a tag, but plan has neither a tag input nor a requirement to return its assigned tag.
findings.failure_scenario: plan prints only the required entity positions and succeeds, leaving the caller without the identifier needed to lint, build, prove, or remove that plan.

findings.claim: Walk and build have no defined failure or completion behavior when pathfinding cannot reach a destination or build position.
findings.failure_scenario: A ghost across water or behind enclosed machinery passes placement checks, but build waits indefinitely for Claude to reach it or terminates after partial construction without identifying what remains unbuilt.

findings.claim: Tick-dependent actions have no specified behavior when invoked while the hosted game is paused.
findings.failure_scenario: After inspecting ghosts while paused, build starts walking but never progresses, or automatically unpauses the entire hosted game and leaves it running; the spec supplies no acceptance condition deciding either behavior.

findings.claim: The end-to-end criterion references an undefined burner-smelting stamp and unspecified starting supplies, output location, and operating conditions.
findings.failure_scenario: Engineers choose different layouts and fuel quantities, so one furnace is working at tick 600 while another valid layout has exhausted fuel or filled its output; there is no common fixture that determines whether the implementation passes.
